question: What are the best alternatives to the ALLPOWERS R600?
query: best alternatives to ALLPOWERS R600 portable power station comparison specs price 2026

replays.text:
The best alternative depends on whether you want something **similar in size** or a **meaningful runtime upgrade**:

- **Closest match: [BLUETTI Elite 30 V2](https://www.itechguides.com/allpowers-r600-portable-power-station-review-a-compact-600w-station-with-one-big-limitation/)** — Its 288Wh capacity and 600W output are close to the R600’s 299Wh and 600W, so it’s the most direct comparison. The cited listing shows it at $279.99; check current pricing before buying.

- **More capacity for the money: [ALLPOWERS S700](https://iallpowers.com/pages/product-compare)** — It offers 606Wh and 700W, roughly twice the R600’s capacity and a little more output. The trade-offs listed are a 100W maximum AC input and a ternary-lithium battery rather than the R600’s LiFePO4 battery. The comparison page lists it from $179, though prices can change.

- **Best substantial step-up: [ALLPOWERS P1800](https://www.itechguides.com/allpowers-r600-portable-power-station-review-a-compact-600w-station-with-one-big-limitation/)** — With 1,024Wh and 1,800W output, it’s much better suited than the R600 to longer backup or larger loads. It’s also heavier—about 28.7 lb—so less convenient for frequent carrying.

- **For expandable backup: [EcoFlow DELTA 2](https://www.itechguides.com/allpowers-r600-portable-power-station-review-a-compact-600w-station-with-one-big-limitation/)** — The review describes it as a 1,024Wh, 1,800W station with capacity expandable up to 3kWh. Consider it if you may want to grow your backup setup later.

**My short take:** Pick the Elite 30 V2 to stay near the R600’s compact format; pick the S700 for more capacity at a listed low price; choose the P1800 or DELTA 2 if runtime is the reason you’re replacing the R600. The R600’s 299Wh battery is its main constraint, so a higher watt rating alone won’t give you longer run time.

The **best alternatives depend on whether you want R600-like portability or more runtime**:

- **BLUETTI Elite 30 V2 — best like-for-like alternative.** It’s close in battery size at **288Wh**, matches the R600’s **600W output**, and adds a claimed **1,500W Power Lifting** mode and 10ms UPS. Consider it for camping, electronics, or brief backup; it won’t solve the R600’s limited-runtime drawback. ([TechRadar review](https://www.techradar.com/pro/bluetti-elite-30-v2-portable-power-station-review); [comparison and listed price](https://www.itechguides.com/allpowers-r600-portable-power-station-review-a-compact-600w-station-with-one-big-limitation/))

- **ALLPOWERS S700 — best budget step-up in capacity.** The ALLPOWERS comparison lists **606Wh and 700W**, roughly twice the R600’s capacity and a little more output. The trade-off: it uses a different battery chemistry than the R600’s LiFePO4, and the listing specifies a lower cycle-life figure. ([ALLPOWERS model comparison](https://iallpowers.com/pages/product-compare))

- **EcoFlow DELTA 2 — best if you need substantially more backup.** It moves up to **1,024Wh and 1,800W**, with capacity expandable up to 3kWh. That’s a much larger, more capable class of station than the R600, rather than a compact substitute. ([R600 comparison and alternatives](https://www.itechguides.com/allpowers-r600-portable-power-station-review-a-compact-600w-station-with-one-big-limitation/))

**My pick:** Get the **Elite 30 V2** if you want a close substitute; choose the **S700** for longer runtime at a similar portability level; step up to the **DELTA 2** for appliances or longer outages. Remember that wattage is what a station can power, while watt-hours determine how long it can run.

The best alternative depends on whether you want a near-like-for-like swap or more runtime:

- **[BLUETTI Elite 30 V2](https://www.techradar.com/pro/bluetti-elite-30-v2-portable-power-station-review)** — **Closest match.** It has 288Wh of LiFePO₄ capacity and 600W output, much like the R600’s 299Wh and 600W. The search results also list a 10ms UPS function and 45-minute charge to 80%. It’s the one I’d compare first if you want a compact station in the same class.
- **[ALLPOWERS S700](https://iallpowers.com/pages/product-compare)** — **More capacity for less, if the listed deal holds.** The manufacturer comparison lists 606Wh and 700W, at a sale price from $179. The trade-off: it uses ternary lithium rather than LiFePO₄, and its listed solar input is lower than the R600’s.
- **[EcoFlow DELTA 2](https://www.itechguides.com/allpowers-r600-portable-power-station-review-a-compact-600w-station-with-one-big-limitation/)** — **Best if the R600’s short runtime is the problem.** It has 1,024Wh, 1,800W output, and expandable capacity, so it’s a more substantial—and less compact—step up.
- **[ALLPOWERS P1800](https://www.itechguides.com/allpowers-r600-portable-power-station-review-a-compact-600w-station-with-one-big-limitation/)** — **A larger-capacity option within the same brand:** 1,024Wh and 1,800W, with LiFePO₄ chemistry.

**My pick:** the Elite 30 V2 for the closest alternative; the DELTA 2 if you need to run devices longer or handle larger loads. The R600’s 299Wh capacity is its main limitation, so for refrigerator or extended outage backup, I’d favor a 1,000Wh-class model. Prices and availability can change.
